page.overview:
Who is Becklespinax?

Becklespinax (now scientifically synonymous with Altispinax), is a genus of theropod dinosaur, that lived during the Early Cretaceous in what is now England.

The Becklespinax clones have an appearance based on recent depictions by paleontologists that resemble Concavenator. Like many of the cloned theropods, they have pronated wrists. The clones also have large white spines sticking out from the back of their necks and a small sail on their back. One of them is colored jaded green with a red face, a yellow neck, and black markings; the other is colored various shades of brown, with splotchy darker markings on its snout.

The Becklespinax was shown to be a formidable hunter that doesn't seem to give up on its prey, as even when one was distracted by a hologram, it refocused a short while after. However, they were willing to give up if they are stuck in a river due to the risk of drowning. The Becklespinax was shown being able to coexist with herbivorous dinosaurs in the same enclosure like Brachiosaurus, Parasaurolophus, Gallimimus, and Stegosaurus without attacking them. Albeit, this is probably due to the watering hole in the center of the enclosure, as both herbivorous and carnivorous dinosaurs have been show to coexist in such areas such as this. Despite this seemingly passive nature, Becklespinax have an aggressive temperament at times, especially towards other predators, as one is shown to attack a T. rex hologram despite believing it to be that actual creature.

These animals are also notable for being able to hold their breath for a surprising amount of time. As one individual was able to survive underwater for a short period of time without oxygen. Possibly hinting at a somewhat semi-aquatic nature.
